body:
Findings from a read of `origin/main` (7a626a7f5). Nothing was built or run.

- The removal during playback is the f64 CPU cut in `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_batch.rs` (`cut_batch`, `cut_brick`). `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs` `seek` drives it. The worker in `crates/app/src/stock_play_worker.rs` packs the lattice each 50 ms.
- The GPU only draws (`crates/ui/src/trace.wgsl`). It removes no material.
- The f32 CPU twin of #2626 has no caller on the playback path. Only `crates/sim/tests/stock_cut_twin.rs` uses it.
- The grid default is 262,144 texels (`DEFAULT_TEXELS`, `stock_view.rs`). The 3D Pocket fixture (70 x 70 x 27 mm) gets a cell of about 0.8 mm.
- No reading of ms for each playing frame or for each move is recorded. The one fig8 reading is a paused frame of 3.4 ms (#2238). The bench `play_bench_tests.rs` times only the UI side on a 100 mm face.
- The held branch of #2620 has the `camcraft-gpu` crate with the probe and the shared device. It has no removal kernel: #2627 writes it.

Owed: a measurement on the fig8 2D Offset and on one 3D Pocket (cells, moves, ms for each frame and for each cut). The recipe is to extend `play_bench_tests.rs`: time `FieldPlay::seek` for each chunk, read `CutStats`, and time `pack_cut`. A worker runs it when a build slot is free.

Codex (m3) read this issue for a pick. It did not claim the issue. Nothing was built.

- This issue is an umbrella. Its fix is #2620, then #2627, then #2629.
- #2620 has a live claim (2026-11-22T09:48Z, branch `issue/2620-gpu-compute-seam`). #2627 and #2629 need #2620 first.
- The counter law "a still frame cuts nothing" already holds on upstream/main 174584111. `FieldPlay::seek` returns `Ok(false)` when `k == at` (`crates/app/src/stock_play.rs`), and `moves_cut()` does not change. A pin for it passes on unchanged code, so it cannot pin a fix.
- The measurement (plan step 1) is a bench, not a failing test. A worker can run it with the recipe in the first comment.

Suggestion: keep this issue open as the tracker. Work #2620, #2627 and #2629 in that order.

Playback cost readings for #3365. The bench is `crates/app/tests/stock_play_cost_bench.rs` (PR #3385).

- Machine: Intel Core i9-10980XE, 3.00 GHz, 18 cores, 36 threads, Windows 11.
- Commit: `origin/main` b6a3e7c6b plus the bench file only (branch head 55eecd47d).
- Each value is the median of three runs. The bench runs alone (`--test-threads=1`).
- Budget: `DEFAULT_TEXELS` (262,144), as playback uses it. The lattice of `PackedBase` holds more texels than the budget, because the region has a margin around the stock.
- The walk is the worker's play mode: a chunk of moves (`FieldPlay::seek`, the worker's chunk law with a 15 ms target), then one publication (`take_dirty`, `view`, then `pack_cut_patch`, or `pack_cut` when the patch is not smaller). A whole-layer `pack_cut` is also timed on each 8th chunk.

Fixtures:

- fig8: `testdata/models/fig8.step`, 2D Offset (the fig8 Adaptive heights, retyped), EM-0800-4FL. Stock 100 x 140 x 22 mm, centred on the part. I chose this stock: it is the part box (85 x 123.6 mm) with about 7.5 mm on each side.
- Pocket: `testdata/models/Milling-test.step`, 3D Pocket, OffsetRings, EM-1000-4FL, stock 70 x 70 x 27 mm from Z -7 (the `pocket3d_hsm.rs` setup).

| Reading | fig8 release | fig8 debug | Pocket release | Pocket debug |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lattice dims, texels per layer | 108 x 145 x 33 = 516,780 | same | 100 x 100 x 47 = 470,000 | same |
| Cell | 1.055 mm | same | 0.796 mm | same |
| Moves in the program | 2,670 | 2,670 | 4,658 | 4,658 |
| Moves walked | 2,670 | 1,823 (stop at 90 s) | 4,658 | 2,904 (stop at 90 s) |
| Cut, ms for each move | 15.12 | 32.95 | 5.53 | 19.58 |
| Cut, moves each second | 66 | 30 | 181 | 51 |
| Cut chunk (`seek`), mean ms / moves in a chunk | 32.8 / 2.2 | 44.0 / 1.3 | 25.0 / 4.5 | 29.0 / 1.5 |
| `pack_cut_patch`, ms (bytes) | 0.19 (about 18 kB) | 1.37 | 0.16 (about 16 kB) | 1.25 |
| `pack_cut` whole layer, ms (bytes) | 14.07 (2,067,120 B) | 165.4 | 9.73 (1,880,000 B) | 132.1 |
| `take_dirty` + `view`, ms | 0.09 | 0.14 | 0.01 | 0.02 |
| Share of one publication: cut / pack / view | 99 % / 1 % / 0 % | 97 % / 3 % / 0 % | 99 % / 1 % / 0 % | 96 % / 4 % / 0 % |

Cut counters for each move (release, run 1): fig8 11,116 cells evaluated, 43.8 bricks touched. Pocket 15,456 cells evaluated, 65.9 bricks touched.

Growth with the cell count (release, median of three, `DEFAULT_TEXELS` at 1/4, 1/2 and 1/1):

| Fixture | Texels | Cell | Cut ms for each move | `pack_cut` ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fig8 | 181,584 | 1.675 mm | 6.89 | 4.66 |
| fig8 | 301,136 | 1.329 mm | 9.58 | 7.95 |
| fig8 | 516,780 | 1.055 mm | 15.12 | 14.07 |
| Pocket | 157,216 | 1.264 mm | 3.83 | 3.18 |
| Pocket | 262,236 | 1.003 mm | 4.49 | 5.81 |
| Pocket | 470,000 | 0.796 mm | 5.53 | 9.73 |

Facts:

- The cut dominates. It is 96 % to 99 % of each publication, in debug and in release. The patch pack is 1 % in release. `take_dirty` and `view` are less than 0.2 ms.
- The upload is not timed (the bench has no GPU device). A play publication sends one patch of about 15 to 19 kB. A whole layer is 1.9 to 2.1 MB.
- Cell count: 2.85 times the texels gives 2.2 times the cut cost for each move on fig8, and 3.0 times the texels gives 1.44 times on the Pocket. The whole-layer `pack_cut` grows about linearly with the texels (3.0 times on fig8, 3.1 times on the Pocket).
- Move count: on fig8 the cost for each move increases along the program. In release it is 6.6 to 8.2 ms in the first quarter of the moves and 17.9 to 22.6 ms in the last quarter. On the Pocket it does not increase (2.7 to 8.8 ms in each quarter, no trend).
- Single chunks: in release run 1, the slowest chunk took 2,997 ms on the Pocket (12 % of the cut wall time) and 2,226 ms on fig8 (7 %). The chunk law gives a chunk of one move or more, so these chunks hold one or few heavy moves.
- 10 ms frame budget: in release, one fig8 move takes 15.1 ms. That is 1.5 times the budget for one move. One Pocket move takes 5.5 ms, so a frame holds about 1.8 moves. The whole-layer `pack_cut` takes 9.7 ms (Pocket) and 14.1 ms (fig8). This is the cost of a repack on the render thread (`eye.rs` `full_cut`), and it is near the budget or more than the budget. In debug each value is 2 to 14 times larger.

How to run: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --release --test stock_play_cost_bench -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`. Each test prints a `SUMMARY|...` line.

Codex (m3) read this issue for a pick on upstream/main e313aa663. It did not claim the issue. Nothing was built.

- #2620 and #2627 are closed. The GPU removal kernel is on main.
- The remaining fix of this issue is #2629 (S3: viewport playback cuts on the GPU). #2629 is P2, effort:high, and has no claim.
- The bench of PR #3385 shows that the cut is 96 % to 99 % of each publication. The cut walk in `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field_batch.rs` already skips full and clear bricks. A read found no CPU quick win that a failing test can pin.
- The counter law "a still frame cuts nothing" already holds (see the comment of 2026-11-22T10:12Z). A pin for it passes on unchanged code.

Suggestion: dispatch #2629 next. Keep this issue open as the tracker until #2629 merges.

Codex (m3) read this issue for a pick on 2026-11-24. It did not claim the issue. Nothing was built.

- This issue is the tracker. The fix is #2629 (S3).
- Two slices of #2629 are merged: PR #3878 (S3a, the GPU keyframe layer cut) and PR #3882 (S3b, the opt-in layer mode of the playback worker).
- #2629 is still open. The remaining S3 work belongs on #2629, not here.
- This issue has no separate code fix. A pin for "a still frame cuts nothing" passes on unchanged code (see the comment of 2026-11-22T10:12Z).

Suggestion: keep this issue open until #2629 closes. Then take a new reading with `crates/app/tests/stock_play_cost_bench.rs` and close this issue on that evidence. The maintainer decides.
